assessment_summary:
Step 7 states a true property (the longest path in this orientation of H has exactly k vertices) even though the greedy backtracking construction it describes requires a Kempe chain argument to prove it doesn't get stuck. 

However, Step 8 contains a fatal mathematical flaw. It claims that extending the orientation to the rest of G arbitrarily cannot create paths longer than k because "no longer path exists in H". This reasoning completely ignores that paths in G can leave H. If G contains additional vertices and edges outside H (for instance, a long path attached to the end of the k-vertex path in H), an arbitrary orientation of these additional edges could easily extend the directed path, resulting in a longest path in G with strictly more than k vertices. Therefore, the described construction fails to guarantee that the longest path in G consists of exactly k vertices.
